questions.q: Can a single Eventstream feed more than one destination at once?
options: Yes — the same source can fan out to multiple destinations, like a KQL Database and a Lakehouse, without duplicating the source
No, each Eventstream is limited to exactly one destination
Only if the destinations are the same item type
Only for batch-ingested sources, never streaming ones
questions.explain: Every destination reads from the same upstream source; nothing about the source changes to make this work.

A way to duplicate a single event into two identical copies
A KQL Database partitioning strategy
A Fabric Capacity billing feature
questions.explain: Each filter feeds a different destination, letting different events take different paths.

questions.q: What idea from Lesson 34 does conditional split routing build on?
options: Routing genuinely out-of-order or anomalous events somewhere separate for review, rather than mixing them into the main flow
The watermark tolerance setting
The bin() function for tumbling windows
The join kind=leftouter operator
questions.explain: Lesson 34 previewed sending problematic events elsewhere; this lesson gives that idea its full mechanism.

questions.q: What does the "needs-review" branch in this lesson's routing design set up for the next lesson?
options: Activator (Lesson 37), which builds real-time alerting on top of routed events
A Power BI Direct Lake report
A Fabric Warehouse stored procedure
The KQL time series functions from Lesson 26
questions.explain: Routing is the mechanism; alerting is what you do with what got routed there.

questions.q: Why is one Eventstream with three destination branches cheaper to run than three separate Eventstreams reading the same source?
options: It reads the source once and branches downstream, rather than paying for the source connection three times and maintaining three definitions in sync
Separate Eventstreams are always free, so there's no cost difference
Multiple destinations always require multiple sources regardless of design
Fan-out is not actually possible in Fabric Eventstreams
questions.explain: There's only one place to update when the source schema changes, instead of three.
